summary: Full backend+frontend testing of new Quick Expense feature. Created /app/backend/tests/test_quick_expense.py with 22 test cases covering parser edge cases, account matching, no-default handling, transaction creation + balance mutation + dashboard reflect, security (cross-family PRIVATE account access), preferences PATCH (200/403/404), recent list scoping, and auth regression. Result: 21/22 passing. One real bug found: GET /api/auth/me does NOT include default_expense_account_id field despite the spec stating it should. Frontend UI /quick-expense verified end-to-end via Playwright: auto-focus, live preview, Enter submit, Escape clear, success flash (qe-success), input clear + focus return, recent list refresh, example chip fill, account-fallback picker when no default, and override flow (default=BNI but hint=gopay → GoPay wins on preview and submit).

critical.issue: Response is missing default_expense_account_id field. The _serialize_user helper in routes/auth.py adds this field for /register and /login responses, but /me returns the raw user dict from auth_utils.get_current_user() which never includes this key (new users are inserted without it). Spec explicitly requires this field on /me. Frontend also relies on prefs endpoint separately so functional UI still works, but this is a contract violation.

action_items: Fix GET /api/auth/me to include default_expense_account_id. Options: (a) refactor /me to re-fetch and pass through _serialize_user, or (b) initialise default_expense_account_id=None on user document at register time so get_current_user naturally returns it. Option (b) is cleaner and also fixes legacy users via a one-off migration.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py: /me endpoint bypasses _serialize_user, so any new user-level field added there is silently missing from /me responses. Consider making get_current_user or /me the single source of truth for the serialized shape.
routes/quick_expense.py create_quick_expense: uses ObjectId(str(acct['_id'])) — double conversion is redundant since acct['_id'] is already an ObjectId; harmless but noisy.

routes/quick_expense.py account matching: exact-match only (case-insensitive) — good, minimises ambiguity. However there is no test for a name-vs-provider tie (e.g. account named 'GoPay' + another with provider 'GoPay') where name-match wins by design. Consider adding a targeted test if that edge is important.

routes/preferences.py: patch treats empty-string as 'clear', but PATCH schema declares Optional[str]=None so client sending null would be a no-op. Empty-string vs null semantics are inconsistent with typical REST — consider documenting.

QuickExpense.jsx duplicates the entire parser and matcher client-side. Fine for live preview, but any divergence will confuse users (e.g. if backend later supports 'juta' suffix, frontend won't). Consider factoring parser into a shared spec or letting backend /parse be the single authority (debounced).
recent_quick_expenses loads all family accounts into memory to enrich response — fine for small families but O(N) per call; could be limited to distinct account_ids from the returned tx rows.
test_credentials: Per-run fresh users. Backend: qe_a+<epoch>@family.id and qe_b+<epoch>@family.id / secret123. UI: qeui+<epoch>@family.id / secret123.
seed_data_creation: Backend test file creates two users in two separate families, each with 0-3 accounts (BNI/GoPay/Cash for user A). Test data auto-created per run — no cleanup required since emails are unique per epoch.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run new suite with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_quick_expense.py -n 0 -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/quick_expense_results.xml. Existing regression suite /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py should still pass (not re-run this iteration; consider re-running after the /me fix lands). Frontend data-testids present and stable: quick-expense-page, qe-input, qe-preview, qe-submit, qe-success, qe-recent, qe-account-fallback, qe-pick-account, qe-set-default, qe-example-{first-word}. Override flow verified: when default is BNI and user types 'kopi 25000 gopay', preview and posted tx both use GoPay.
rca of the issue: Bug: /me missing default_expense_account_id. RCA: routes/auth.py defines _serialize_user() to include the new field, which is applied ONLY on /register and /login return paths. The /me endpoint (`return current_user`) uses the dict produced by auth_utils.get_current_user, which does raw MongoDB read + strip of _id/password_hash. Because new users are inserted without a default_expense_account_id key (only set later via PATCH /preferences), the field is entirely absent from /me responses until it is written for the first time. Reproduction: register any new user, call GET /api/auth/me → 'default_expense_account_id' key missing from JSON. Mitigation: either (a) rewrite /me to `return _serialize_user(await db.users.find_one({_id: ObjectId(current_user['id'])}))`, or (b) set default_expense_account_id=None in both register paths of auth.py (Path A invited user + Path B new owner) and add a light migration.
